REQ-RESET: DMA request, interrupt and both grants are clear after reset.
REQ-HOLD: An offered write keeps its owner, address and data stable until accepted.
REQ-ARBITRATE: The arbiter never grants both requesters at once.
REQ-PRIORITY: On a new, unstalled arbitration with both requests pending, CPU wins (baseline). The alternate policy gives DMA priority.
REQ-DATA: Both DMA writes and the CPU write reach their expected addresses and leave an untouched address unchanged.
REQ-IRQ: The DMA signals completion exactly once, only after its second accepted write, and deasserts the interrupt.
REQ-MEMORY: The isolated memory returns reset data, then returns the accepted write.
